newsitem.title: HUNGARY: CSFB says TVK cheap, rates it a 'buy'.
newsitem.headline: CSFB says TVK cheap, rates it a 'buy'.

text.p: CS First Boston (CSFB) said the Hungarian chemicals maker Tiszai Vegyi Kombinat (TVK) was one of the cheapest in the European chemicals sector and rated it a "buy".

"We see TVK as a stock which is sharply undervalued on fundamentals while being held back by (temporary) technical considerations," Budapest-based CSFB analyst Jakab L. Spencer said in a company update.
He said TVK appeared to be roughly 60 percent undervalued and was the cheapest stock in the Western and Eastern European chemicals sector after the Czech Republic's MCHZ.
"One of those technical hurdles may have been overcome with the local sale of a 10.5 percent block in TVK," he added.
Press reports said last week that Tiszaujvaros, the local municipality where the TVK plant is located, had sold its 10.5 percent stake in TVK. The price and name of the buyer have not been published.

"The deal should give some breathing room to the share price, which has been depressed due to mainly technical rather than fundamental factors, not least by the huge share package being openly offered to several local and foreign investors over the last three months," Spencer said.
CSFB said that TVK was made highly competitive by its low cost of production.

It said a shift in TVK's sales towards the domestic market was a positive sign for TVK for which its relatively remote location from Europe's main chemicals and plastic producers and its landlocked site meant high transport cost on export products.

"Domestic sales during the period (Q1-Q3 1996) rose to 53 percent of total versus 48 percent during the same period last year, reflecting strengthening demand for commodity chemicals in Eastern Europe," Spencer said.

"We estimate that for each two percentage point shift to the domestic market TVK gains one percent in EPS relative to the status quo," he said, adding that domestic selling margins were about 10 to 12 percent higher than export margins.

Profitability levels for TVK remained acceptable in the past year though the margins for ethylene, propylene and various polimers (LDPE), PP, HDPE) have narrowed considerably from their high point of a year ago, he said.
